title: Notification pods restarting
summary: Notification‑service pods began OOM‑killing at ~07:50 UTC after the v3.9.2 deploy at 07:12 UTC introduced per‑recipient‑locale template caching. Memory utilization climbed from 0.55 to >0.97, GC overhead hit ~37 % CPU, and consumer lag grew from ~128 to >53 k messages. The critic accepted HYP‑1 (cache‑leak regression, change chg:2591) as the root cause with high confidence (0.85). The investigation is conclusive, but a heap dump or allocation‑rate metric to directly observe the leaking cache map has not yet been captured.

hypothesis.mechanism: The v3.9.2 deploy added per‑recipient‑locale template caching. The cache retains strong references without eviction, causing a steady heap increase. Rising heap triggers frequent GC (≈37 % CPU), then OOMKills, pod restarts, and growing consumer lag as the consumer repeatedly crashes.
predictions: Heap dump from a pod before OOM shows a large map keyed by locale holding compiled templates.
Disabling the locale cache (feature flag) stops memory growth.

objections.detail: The cache‑leak mechanism assumes the locale cache holds strong references without eviction; a heap dump or allocation‑rate metric would confirm this, but such data is not currently available.

hypothesis.mechanism: An unrecorded upstream change (e.g., a feature flag or marketing campaign) increased the rate or payload size of messages published to the notification Kafka topics. The consumer buffers whole batches in heap, so the sudden surge drives memory pressure, GC overhead, OOMKills, and a massive consumer‑lag backlog.
predictions: Orders‑service or payments‑service producer metrics show a sharp rise in msg/sec or avg payload bytes around 07:30‑07:45.
Kafka broker logs show increased fetch latency or partition lag at the same time.

objections.detail: The hypothesis ignores contradictory observations: no upstream deploy/config changes (OBS‑3), empty upstream dependency list (OBS‑4), no Kafka‑related logs in orders‑service (OBS‑12), and memory growth precedes any plausible traffic surge (OBS‑8, OBS‑7).

facts.statement: deploy on notification-service at 07:12:30 UTC by ci/deploy-bot: notification-service v3.9.2: cache rendered templates per recipient locale (version: 3.9.2, previous_version: 3.9.1, commit: 0f6c3a8, diff: +88 / -21)
notification-service was deployed to version 3.9.2 at 07:12:30 UTC (commit 0f6c3a8, diff +88/-21).
No changes were recorded for orders-service, payments-service, or kafka in the 07:00–08:20 UTC window.
The upstream dependency query for notification-service returned an empty dependency list, indicating no recorded producers in the dependency graph.
Deploy of notification-service v3.9.2 completed at 07:12:30 UTC.
GC overhead high warnings (≈37 % time in GC) start at 07:35:06 and continue through 08:19.
Memory utilization rises from baseline 0.55 (07:00) to 0.63 at 07:18, 0.78 at 07:33, 0.91 at 07:45, and exceeds 0.97 by 07:51.
First OOMKill of a notification-service pod recorded at 07:52:13; subsequent kills at 07:55, 07:58, 08:01, … up to 08:19.
Consumer lag metric jumps from baseline mean 128 messages to a peak of 53 710 messages; last observed value 53 110 at 08:20.
Error rate rises from baseline 0.002 to 0.034 by 08:20; latency p99 modestly increases from 252 ms baseline to 249 ms last (within normal range).
Log pattern searches for “kafka” and “notification” in orders‑service returned zero matches for the 07:00‑08:20 UTC window.

assumptions.statement: The new per‑locale template cache retains objects indefinitely (no eviction or size bound).
assumptions.reason: The code change adds caching but no explicit TTL or max‑entries were mentioned; typical pattern leads to unbounded growth.

assumptions.statement: No other configuration or feature‑flag change touched notification‑service between 07:00‑08:20 UTC.
assumptions.reason: Change history for the window only records the v3.9.2 deploy (OBS‑1/2/6).

assumptions.statement: An unrecorded upstream change (feature flag, campaign, data feed) could have altered message volume or size.
assumptions.reason: Responder notes reference a prior marketing‑campaign incident; such campaigns often launch without a deploy.

assumptions.statement: Notification consumer buffers full batches in heap before processing.
assumptions.reason: Common Kafka consumer implementations accumulate records in memory; a sudden payload increase would manifest as heap growth.

actions.description: Roll back notification‑service to v3.9.1 or disable the locale‑cache feature flag to stop OOM kills immediately.
actions.rationale: The memory leak is triggered by the new cache; removing the change halts the impact while a permanent fix is built.

actions.description: Add eviction (e.g., size‑bounded LRU or weak references) to the locale template cache and verify memory stability under load.
actions.rationale: Eliminates the unbounded strong‑reference map that causes steady heap growth.

actions.description: Instrument cache size and GC‑overhead metrics; add alerts for GC > 30 % CPU or memory > 90 % of limit.
actions.rationale: Early detection of similar regressions in future releases.
